response.consequence: Tokens from the client credentials grant, legacy token exchange, UMA and implicit/hybrid flows carry the wrong grant-type marker in their IDs. Consumers or tests that expect a grant-specific token ID for those grants will fail or misclassify the tokens.
response.explanation: The change sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE only in createTokenResponse (authorization code, device, CIBA), the resource owner password grant, pre-authorized code, standard token exchange and refresh. TokenManager.initToken calls DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, which falls back to UNKNOWN ("na") when the attribute is missing. Grep over services/src/main/java shows no GRANT_TYPE assignment before AccessTokenResponseBuilder.generateAccessToken() in ClientCredentialsGrantType (line 140), AbstractTokenExchangeProvider (line 410), AuthorizationTokenService (UMA, line 358) or OIDCLoginProtocol (line 272). The same applies to the direct createClientAccessToken calls in PolicyEvaluationService and KeycloakIdentity. Client credentials, legacy and V1 token exchange, and UMA tokens therefore get an "na" grant-type segment in their token ID. This is inconsistent with the grant-aware ID the change introduces. The caller-supplied grant_type is not a risk here: TokenEndpoint dispatches only to registered grants, and an unregistered value would make encodeTokenId throw IllegalStateException.

response.consequence: A null rawTokenId is accepted. encodeTokenId then builds a token id ending in ":null", and getRawTokenId() can return null. This produces malformed token ids instead of failing early.

response.consequence: No defect confirmed in the supplied code. I did not grep the other getShortcut implementations, so uniqueness across all grant factories is unchecked.
response.explanation: The size check does catch both kinds of collision. If two grants share a shortcut but have different IDs, grantsByShortcuts keeps one entry while grantsToShortcuts keeps two, so the sizes differ and postInit throws. If two grants share an ID but have different shortcuts, the reverse happens and the check also throws. Grants that are not registered at postInit time are handled by the refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut. Those paths look the factory up again and fill both maps, so a missing shortcut does not break token issuance.

response.consequence: The event assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken give false confidence. Token IDs encoded with the wrong grant shortcut would pass undetected. If the offset were fixed without fixing the inversion, the tests would fail for correct tokens.
response.explanation: In isAccessTokenId, the line `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two defects. First, the condition is inverted: it rejects a token ID whose grant shortcut matches the expected one. Second, the offset is wrong. Token IDs look like `ofrtro:5678` or `trltcc:1234`, which are 2 chars of session type, 2 of token type and 2 of grant. The grant shortcut is therefore at index 4 to 6, not 3 to 5. substring(3,5) returns the last char of the token-type pair plus the first char of the grant pair, for example `tr`. It will practically never equal a 2-char shortcut, so the inverted check never fires. The matcher therefore only verifies the `xxxxxx:<uuid>` shape and never verifies the grant type. A short prefix (fewer than 5 chars before the colon) also makes substring throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning a mismatch.

replacement.original:
// Grant type shortcut starts at character 4th char and is 2-chars long
                if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
replacement.text:
// Grant type shortcut starts at the 5th char (index 4) and is 2-chars long
                if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;

response.title: isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant shortcut: condition inverted and offset wrong

hypotheses.failure_mode: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException for token IDs with a ':' but a malformed or unknown prefix. Any access token whose jti contains ':' (e.g. tokens from other issuers/versions or an unrecognized shortcut) would make introspection, userinfo, or logout validation fail with a 500 instead of a clean invalid-token result. Also, the factory's getGrantTypeByShortcut lazy refresh runs a stream over provider factories on every unknown shortcut, and the plain HashMap swap in tests masks concurrency issues.

The shortcuts 'rt' (RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory) and 'rt' (TokenType.REGULAR) are in different positions, so they do not collide.
